enrichment.fit_reasoning: Kearney Public Schools is a high-priority target. Enrollment of 5,500 sits squarely in Journify's sweet spot. The SPED population (~14%, ~770 IEP students) is above average, creating real documentation and caseload pressure. Most importantly, the named decision-maker — Sandra Bauer, Director of Student Services — self-initiated contact on the same day she attended a Journify webinar, citing a peer referral from Lincoln Public Schools. This is a warm, inbound, peer-influenced lead with a clear evaluation timeline (next school year). No competitor contract signals detected. Only minor uncertainty is around which IEP system of record is currently in use and whether a formal RFP process will be required, which tempers the score slightly below 90.

email_draft.subject: Kearney's 770 IEPs, less paperwork | Journify
email_draft.body:
Sandra, you attended "AI in Special Education: What Actually Works" on March 30 and submitted a contact form the same afternoon mentioning Lincoln Public Schools and Kearney's 14% SPED population.

At roughly 770 students with IEPs, your case managers and related-service providers are carrying a documentation load that competes directly with instruction time. Teachers using Journify report saving more than four hours per day on IEP drafting, present-levels write-ups, and progress notes, and because Journify works alongside your existing IEP system rather than replacing it, the team doesn't start over. Your SLPs, OTs, and SPED teachers work from one shared workflow, so the right people are contributing to each student's plan without duplicating effort.

If you're scoping options for 2026, 27, I can have a tailored walk-through on your calendar this week, would Thursday or Friday work for 20 minutes?
email_draft.hook_summary: Same-day webinar attendance + contact form submission on 3/30, citing Lincoln Public Schools peer referral and Kearney's 14% SPED population.
